behaviour.issuerPowers: The owner (0xF68a4b64162906efF0fF6aE34E2bB1Cd42FEf62d when read) can mint any amount and transfer or renounce ownership; holders can burn. No pause, blocklist or fee function. Its value rests on Binance holding the USDT behind it.

checked.how: the functions the runtime dispatches on (PUSH4 scan of the code read from two endpoints: mint(uint256), burn(uint256), owner; no pause, blocklist or fee function); on a loopback fork: transfer, approve and transferFrom return true, approve from 5 to 7 succeeds, transferFrom of 3 received as 3

confirmation.residualRisk: The chain's own fast finality is one or two blocks behind the head, so the page keeps `finalized` for everything, as on the Bloch L2. Residual: fast finality stalling (the page then says so and waits).

openingPrice.minimumReason: At least 0.5 BNB and its USDT (Binance-Peg) at the market price: the same floor as this chain's first pair, for the same reason (gas is negligible here; the floor keeps the pool worth more than a few hundred dollars a side). Inflating the first share is not possible at any size (only the depositing account can mint first, and the pair locks 1,000 share units); the tool also refuses a deposit whose share supply would be under 10^12 units, so that the locked units are at most a billionth of it.

reserveCapsReason: No caps (coordinator's technical decision, 2026-11-17): an ordinary constant-product exchange. The caps exist on the Bloch L2 to bound what a fault of the bridge can drain through a pool of a bridged asset; the assets listed here are the chain's own native coin and a token issued on this chain, so that risk does not exist, and a pool capped on both sides would leak its fees to whoever calls skim first (docs/MULTICHAIN-DEPLOY.md section 2).
